states.verdict: This is not a comparison, it is the same caret twice, shifted one device pixel. Both draw a 3×36 CSS px cyan slab at exactly 1.0× line-height, hard-edged, unmodulated #00B5FF — the only colour on an otherwise #1C1C1C-on-#F9F9F9 page, which reads as a default someone forgot to tune rather than a chosen instrument, and both float it ~2 CSS px past the character cell so it never actually touches the 's' you just typed. B takes it on one point only: it is half a pixel closer to the truth, and it does not let a status bar amputate the caret to 39% height the moment you write to the bottom of the window. Neither image shows a selection — 432 chromatic pixels in the entire frame, all of them caret — so the selection half of this dimension is simply undelivered by both.

states.verdict: These are the same caret with a rounding error between them, and it is a bad caret twice. Six device px wide and 72 px tall — exactly the full 72 px line pitch, 2.57x the 28 px cap height, riding 20 px above the cap line and 24 px below the baseline — so it spans the entire leading and butts into the caret slot of the lines above and below; that is a highlighter slab, not a nib. Worse, it is drawn at #AFE5FB for 1.29:1 contrast on #F9F9F9 while the body text sits at 16.19:1, making the one element that must always be findable the palest thing on the page: you will lose it mid-sentence and hunt for it. Both float ~6 px right of the actual insertion boundary, so neither tells you truthfully where the next letter lands; A is one pixel less wrong, which is the entire case for A.
